L10: # ESP-IDF Versions【1†】
L11: 
L12: 【2†[中文]】
L13: 
L14: The ESP-IDF GitHub repository is updated regularly, especially the master branch where new development takes place.
L15: 
L16: For production use, there are also stable releases available.
L17: ## Releases【3†】
L18: 
L19: The documentation for the current stable release version can always be found at this URL:
L20: 
L21: 【4†https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/】
L22: 
L23: Documentation for the latest version (master branch) can always be found at this URL:
L24: 
L25: 【5†https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/】
L26: The full history of releases can be found on the GitHub repository 【6†Releases page†github.com】. There you can find release notes, links to each version of the documentation, and instructions for obtaining each version.
L27: Another place to find documentation for all current releases is the documentation page, where you can go to the upper-left corner and click the version dropdown (between the target dropdown and the search bar). You can also use this dropdown to switch between versions of the documentation.
L28: 
L29: 【7†Image: _images/choose_version.png】
L30: 
L31: Documentation for older versions are also still available:
L32: ## Which Version Should I Start With?【8†】
L33:   * For production purposes, use the 【4†current stable version】. Stable versions have been manually tested, and are updated with "bugfix releases" which fix bugs without changing other functionality (see 【9†Versioning Scheme】 for more details). Every stable release version can be found on the 【6†Releases page†github.com】.
L34: Also refer to 【10†Compatibility Between ESP-IDF Releases and Revisions of Espressif SoCs†github.com】 to make sure the ESP-IDF version you selected is compatible with the chip revision you are going to produce with.
L35:   * For prototyping, experimentation or for developing new ESP-IDF features, use the 【5†latest version (master branch in Git)】. The latest version in the master branch has all the latest features and has passed automated testing, but has not been completely manually tested ("bleeding edge").
L36:   * If a required feature is not yet available in a stable release, but you do not want to use the master branch, it is possible to check out a pre-release version or a release branch. It is recommended to start from a stable version and then follow the instructions for 【11†Updating to a Pre-Release Version】 or 【12†Updating to a Release Branch】.
L37:   * If you plan to use another project which is based on ESP-IDF, please check the documentation of that project to determine the version(s) of ESP-IDF it is compatible with.
L38: 
L39: See 【13†Updating ESP-IDF】 if you already have a local copy of ESP-IDF and wish to update it.
L40: ## Versioning Scheme【14†】
L41: 
L42: ESP-IDF uses 【15†Semantic Versioning†semver.org】. This means that:
L43: 
L44:   * Major Releases, like `v3.0`, add new functionality and may change functionality. This includes removing deprecated functionality.
L45: 
L46: If updating to a new major release (for example, from `v2.1` to `v3.0`), some of your project's code may need updating and functionality may need to be re-tested. The release notes on the 【6†Releases page†github.com】 include lists of Breaking Changes to refer to.
L47:   * Minor Releases like `v3.1` add new functionality and fix bugs but will not change or remove documented functionality, or make incompatible changes to public APIs.
L48: 
L49: If updating to a new minor release (for example, from `v3.0` to `v3.1`), your project's code does not require updating, but you should re-test your project. Pay particular attention to the items mentioned in the release notes on the 【6†Releases page†github.com】.
L50:   * Bugfix Releases like `v3.0.1` only fix bugs and do not add new functionality.
L51: 
L52: If updating to a new bugfix release (for example, from `v3.0` to `v3.0.1`), you do not need to change any code in your project, and you only need to re-test the functionality directly related to bugs listed in the release notes on the 【6†Releases page†github.com】.
L53: ## Support Periods【16†】
L54: 
L55: Each ESP-IDF major and minor release version has an associated support period. After this period, the release is End of Life and no longer supported.
L56: 
L57: The 【17†ESP-IDF Support Period Policy†github.com】 explains this in detail, and describes how the support periods for each release are determined.
L58: 
L59: Each release on the 【6†Releases page†github.com】 includes information about the support period for that particular release.
L60: 
L61: As a general guideline:
L62:   * If starting a new project, use the latest stable release.
L63: 
L64:   * If you have a GitHub account, click the "Watch" button in the top-right of the 【6†Releases page†github.com】 and choose "Releases only". GitHub will notify you whenever a new release is available. Whenever a bug fix release is available for the version you are using, plan to update to it.
L65:   * If possible, periodically update the project to a new major or minor ESP-IDF version (for example, once a year.) The update process should be straightforward for Minor updates, but may require some planning and checking of the release notes for Major updates.
L66: 
L67:   * Always plan to update to a newer release before the release you are using becomes End of Life.
L68: 
L69: Each ESP-IDF major and minor release (V4.1, V4.2, etc) is supported for 30 months after the initial stable release date.
L70: Supported means that the ESP-IDF team will continue to apply bug fixes, security fixes, etc to the release branch on GitHub, and periodically make new bugfix releases as needed.
L71: 
L72: Support period is divided into "Service" and "Maintenance" period:
L73: 
L74: Period  | Duration  | Recommended for new projects?
L75: --- | --- | ---
L76: Service  | 12 months  | Yes
L77: Maintenance  | 18 months  | No
L78: During the Service period, bugfixes releases are more frequent. In some cases, support for new features may be added during the Service period (this is reserved for features which are needed to meet particular regulatory requirements or standards for new products, and which carry a very low risk of introducing regressions.)
L79: 
L80: During the Maintenance period, the version is still supported but only bugfixes for high severity issues or security issues will be applied.
L81: Using an "In Service" version is recommended when starting a new project.
L82: 
L83: Users are encouraged to upgrade all projects to a newer ESP-IDF release before the support period finishes and the release becomes End of Life (EOL). It is our policy to not continue fixing bugs in End of Life releases.
L84: Pre-release versions (betas, previews, `-rc` and `-dev` versions, etc) are not covered by any support period. Sometimes a particular feature is marked as "Preview" in a release, which means it is also not covered by the support period.
L85: 
L86: The ESP-IDF Programming Guide has information about the 【18†different versions of ESP-IDF】 (major, minor, bugfix, etc).
L87: 
L88: 【19†Image: https://dl.espressif.com/dl/esp-idf/support-periods.svg†dl.espressif.com】
L89: ## Checking the Current Version【20†】
L90: 
L91: The local ESP-IDF version can be checked by using idf.py:
L92: 
L93:     idf.py --version
L94: 
L95: 
L96: The ESP-IDF version is also compiled into the firmware and can be accessed (as a string) via the macro `IDF_VER`. The default ESP-IDF bootloader prints the version on boot (The version information is not always updated if the code in the GitHub repo is updated, it only changes if there is a clean build or if that particular source file is recompiled).
L97: If writing code that needs to support multiple ESP-IDF versions, the version can be checked at compile time using 【21†compile-time macros】.
L98:

L125: ## 159.0 Firefox Release
L126: 
L127: October 27, 2026
L128: 
L129: Version 159.0, first offered to Release channel users on October 27, 2026
L130: 
L131:   * 【46†Previous Firefox 158.0】
L132: ### New
L133: 
L134:   * Sharing on macOS now uses the native macOS share picker, which shows a preview of the page and recent contacts alongside AirDrop, Messages, and other apps. Several selected tabs can also be shared at once.
L135: 
L136: 【47†Image: Screenshot showing the native macOS share picker】
L137: 
L138:   * Saved passwords are now available from the sidebar by default, without having to add the Passwords tool first.
L139: 
L140: 【48†Image: Screenshot showing saved passwords being available in the browser sidebar】
L141:   * 【49†Smart Window】 can now watch pages for changes such as price drops or restocks. Type `/watch` in the chat to set one up, and Firefox sends a desktop notification when it finds a match. Watches can be managed from the Tasks button in the toolbar or the `about:smartwindowtasks` page.
L142: 
L143: 【50†Image】
L144: 
L145: This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
L146: 
L147: What is a progressive roll out?
L148: Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.
L149: ### Fixed
L150: 
L151:   * Fixed the file upload dialog opening in the last folder a file was saved to, such as Downloads, instead of the folder last used for uploads.
L152: 
L153:   * Fixed memory usage growing rapidly when sites such as the Zoom web app were left open in a minimized window.
L154: 
L155:   * Fixed some videos displaying incorrectly on Windows when NVIDIA RTX Video HDR is enabled.
L156: 
L157:   * Fixed bookmarks not being imported from Google Chrome profiles that are signed in to a Google account.
L158:   * Fixed the Replace button in Apple Writing Tools on macOS inserting the clipboard contents instead of the rewritten text on some sites, such as Gmail.
L159: 
L160:   * Fixed long drop-down lists on web pages sometimes showing blank space in place of the last options until the list was scrolled.
L161: 
L162:   * Fixed some sites, such as Slack, failing to load instead of falling back to HTTP/2 when the site rejected an HTTP/3 request.
L163:   * Fixed Firefox using excessive memory on Linux with AMD graphics when viewing map or place results on sites such as ChatGPT.
L164: 
L165:   * Fixed quick gamepad button presses sometimes being missed in web games on macOS.
L166: 
L167:   * Fixed tabs sometimes detaching into a new window when clicked on Linux with Wayland.
L168: 
L169:   * Fixed menus and panels fading in on Windows and Linux when animation effects are turned off in the operating system.
L170: 
L171:   * Various 【51†security fixes†www.mozilla.org】.
L172: ### Changed
L173: 
L174:   * On macOS, apps that sign in through the default browser, such as ChatGPT, now open their sign-in page in Firefox instead of Safari when Firefox is the default browser.
L175: 
L176:   * The 【52†AI chatbot's†support.mozilla.org】 Summarize page option now sends the page's address to the chatbot provider instead of the page's text, so long pages are no longer cut short to a partial summary.
L177:   * Open tabs can now be searched with a keyboard shortcut: `Ctrl+Shift+A` on Windows and Linux, `Cmd+Shift+A` on macOS. The Extensions and Themes shortcut is now `Ctrl+Shift+F` on Windows and Linux, and `Cmd+Shift+E` on macOS. These shortcuts can be changed in `about:keyboard`.
L178: 
L179:   * Web addresses written in the Javanese, Balinese, Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics, and N'Ko scripts are now displayed in their own script instead of as encoded "xn--" text.
L180: ### Enterprise
L181: 
L182:   * For Firefox Enterprise updates and fixes, see the 【53†Firefox Enterprise release notes】. For policy changes, see the 【54†Firefox admin docs changelog†firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org】.
L183: 
L184: ### Developer
L185: 
L186:   * 【55†Developer Information†developer.mozilla.org】
L187: 
L188:   * The Web Console now allows `let`, `const`, and `class` variables to be declared again, so a snippet can be edited and re-run without a redeclaration error.
L189: ### Web Platform
L190: 
L191:   * Firefox now supports 【56†scroll-driven animations†developer.mozilla.org】, so CSS animations and Web Animations API animations can progress with the scroll position of a container or with an element's visibility as it scrolls into view. This adds the `animation-timeline`, `scroll-timeline`, `view-timeline`, and `animation-range` properties and the `ScrollTimeline` and `ViewTimeline` interfaces.

L42: # General Highlights and UX Improvements【14†⁠】
L43: 
L44: A number of the fixes we first mentioned in our 【30†last development update】 were backported to GIMP 3.2.6.
L45: 
L46: Cheesequake has added code so you can use Cut on a layer group. This will allow you to cut the same section of all layers in the group, provided they are rasterized and not locked. Jehan made further improvements to this code.
L47: The `Sample Merged` option for the Color Picker tool should now include any filters applied to a single layer when selecting colors. This was originally ignored due to an older optimization used for single layer images.
L48: 
L49: Balooii made many improvements to boost performance when loading a large number of fonts. While some lag remains and will likely require us to update to GTK4, the initial GIMP start-up, typing in the text tool, and closing font lists should be much faster!
L50: Ondřej Míchal and Jehan have begun making changes to GIMP’s codebase to support an eventual GTK4 port. This includes swapping out the deprecated `gtk_widget_show ()` functions with `gtk_widget_set_visible ()`, replacing direct access to `GdkEvent` types with getter functions, replacing `GDK_WA_CURSOR` flags for explicit `gdk_window_set_cursor ()` calls, and more. Even though we are not yet planning a GTK4 port, it doesn’t hurt to start preparing for it!
L51: New contributor Ryan McDonald and Idriss Fekir have fixed an issue where the end of a line might be hidden on the left/right side when the text layout is set to “fixed”. When loading older XCFs, the problem will still be visible, but any changes to the text layer will update it to the correct view.
L52: 
L53: Kaushik B. has fixed an issue with the 【31†Heal Tool†docs.gimp.org】 where you might get dark smudges if you move outside the bounds of a layer that’s smaller than the image canvas.
L54: New contributor Manu Cornet and Jehan fixed a crash that could happen in certain circumstances when pressing keys too quickly after releasing the spacebar when panning.
L55: 
L56: Brandon Henderson reduced the sensitivity of the pan gestures when using the touchpad on macOS. This should make it easier to make fine-grain adjustments while editing an image on that platform!
L57: 
L58: Richard Gitschlag has adjusted the Text Tool so that you can still select the text to edit even if it has a layer mask that partially covers it.
L59: Jacob Boerema resolved a bug in our metadata code that prevented GIMP from loading the Licensor metadata for an image.
L60: 
L61: Alx Sa added a maximum width of tooltips, preventing options with long descriptions from filling the entire screen.
L62: 
L63: Rodrigo Lledó Milanca updated our information on the 【32†ART†artraweditor.github.io】 Camera RAW plug-ins.
L64: 
L65: Several bugs related to rasterized vector layers have been resolved. Thanks to BobsDaughter, teapot, and Richard Gitschlag for their testing and feedback!
L66: # New Rotation Stylus Dynamics Input【15†⁠】
L67: 
L68: Jehan recently implemented a new dynamic input for painting - `Rotation` (also known as `Barrel Rotation`). This feature is prominently used in the original Wacom Art Pen and newer Wacom Art Pen 2 pens, and allows GIMP to react to how you have rotated the brush in your hand as you draw.
L69: You can adjust this value for custom brushes in the 【33†Dynamics editor†docs.gimp.org】. The MyPaint Brush tool is integrated with this feature as well, so it will automatically pass the rotation on as you paint if your stylus supports it.
L70: # OS and Platform Specific Improvements【16†⁠】
L71: 
L72: GIMP uses 【34†GTK3†www.gtk.org】, a cross-platform library for GUIs, to display its windows, widgets, and more. While it does a very good job of this, GIMP requires a lot of very complex interactions, and sometimes this can expose bugs that are only visible on certain platforms.
L73: 
L74: Bruno Lopes has been hard at work making a staggering number of platform-specific improvements to make GIMP work better. These include (but are not limited to):
L75:   * Using “Server-side Decorations” for dialogs on KDE instead of GNOME-style “Client-side Decorations”. (In other words, the buttons appear at the bottom of the dialog instead of the header bar).
L76: 
L77:   * Secondary “pop-up” windows such as the resource selection and metadata editor dialogs should now appear in front of the first dialogue on Windows and macOS.
L78: 
L79:   * The System theme now uses your system’s defined accent colors on Windows and macOS.
L80:   * Many improvements to proper focus setting on Windows and macOS.
L81: 
L82:   * Improvements to multi-window mode operations on Windows and macOS.
L83: 
L84:   * More system theme leaks caught on KDE Breeze system themes. This should help with graphical glitches in the UI.
L85: 
L86:   * We now depend on `winflexbison` on Windows for building the 【35†Image Map plugin†docs.gimp.org】. This fixes an issue where Windows users couldn’t reopen their image maps, even when created with GIMP.
L87:   * Send to Email now works on MS Windows too using `MAPI` (works with 【36†Thunderbird†www.thunderbird.net】 and Outlook Classic).
L88: 
L89:   * Windows users can now use “Open With” on multiple files on start, without creating multiple instances of GIMP. This is consistent with how Linux and other platforms operate.
L90: Because these improvements are wide-ranging, it is possible that we missed some interactions during testing that could cause a regression. If you notice any problems in GIMP 3.2.6, please 【37†let us know】!
L91: ## New macOS Package【17†⁠】
L92: 
L93: Starting with GIMP 3.2.6, the .dmg package is now created at the same time as the Linux and Windows packages. This has not been possible for many years!
L94: We used to create binaries for macOS on a separate GitLab repository, which was mirrored to another repository on GitHub, which was connected to a proprietary CI service (CircleCI) which then was connected to a MacStadium runner. All of that with dozens and dozens of additional patches, scripts etc! As you can see, this was extremely complicated, but it was the only way to ship macOS binaries back then.
L95: Thanks to your 【38†donations†testing.gimp.org】, we were able to sponsor a MacBook Pro M5 for Bruno Lopes, who has been working since December 19, 2025 to fix that situation. As a result, GIMP can now be easily built on macOS with both MacPorts and Homebrew packages.
L96: 
L97: The macOS version of GIMP is now much more integrated with system-specific features, similar to the Linux and Windows version. A few examples:
L98: 
L99:   * Titlebars on macOS now follow the dark/light mode settings of the current theme.
